JUDGMENT

This is a Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.70,00,000/ for the Death of one Mr.Arun Kumar H.R. in a road traffic accident dated 23.05.2020.
SCCH-25 2

. The case of the Petitioners in brief is that, on 23.05.2020 at about 05.20am the deceased Arunkumar H.R. was going to his garden on the left side of the road, near Kotthipur Bridge, BM Road, NH75, Kunigal, very carefully, cautiously and observing all the traffic rules

, at that time one Goods Canter bearing Reg.No.KA20D3899 driven by its driver at a very high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endangering to human life came from behind and dashed to the deceased.
As a result of which the deceased fell down and sustained severe head injury and other injuries on all over the body and died on the spot.
Thereafter the body of the deceased was shifted to Kunigal Government Hospital to conduct post mortem, after post mortem the dead body handed over to them.

3. It is further case of the petitioners that, prior to the date of accident he was hale and healthy, aged about 22 years, working as a Salesman in the ESSAR OIL LIMITED, Sri Venkateshwara (Essar Bunk) Enterprises and after his SCCH-25 company work he was doing Agriculture in his land and was earning sum of Rs.30,000/ per month from both works and he was the only bread winner and looking after the welfare and all needs of his family and both the petitioners are dependents of his income, due to the sudden demise of the deceased, they suffered irreparable loss, damage and untold miseries throughout their life.
They lost bread winner of their family and they have no other means of income.
So far they have spent Rs.80,000/ towards death related ceremonies and Rs.10,000/ towards transportation of the dead body.
The Kunigal police has registered a case against the driver of the offending vehicle in Cr.No.132/2020.
The 1st respondent is the insurer and 2 nd respondent is the owner of the said vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to them.

sentences.text: In response to the service of notice, the Respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared through their respective counsel and filed separate written statements.
SCCH-25 5.

The respondent No.1 in the written statement has denied the case of the petitioners as false,
admitted issuance of policy subject to terms and conditions and submitted that there is non compliance of 134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
Further submitted that the offending vehicle has been falsely implicated in the case and therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against them.

6. The Respondent No.2 in the written statement has denied the petition averments as false and submitted that the vehicle was maintained regularly in the authorized service station, hence there is no negligence on the part of either the Driver or upon them.
Further submitted that their vehicle duly insured with the respondent No.1 as on the date of accident, driver had valid DL and the vehicle had vehicular documents.
Accordingly, prayed for dismissal of the petition against them.

7. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:
SCCH-25 1. Whether the Petitioners prove that, they are the legal heirs of the deceased Sri.Arun Kumar H.R.?

2. Whether the Petitioners prove that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of the driver of the Goods Canter bearing Reg.No.KA20D3899 as a result Sri.Arun Kumar H.R. sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries?
3. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
4.
What Order or Award?
8. In order to prove the case, the Petitioners have got examined petitioner No.2 - Father of the deceased as PW.1 and got marked 19 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.19.
They have also examined Mr.Ranganath - eye witness as PW.2 and not produce any document.
Mr.Krishnaraja Naidu - Manager (Employer) of the deceased examined as PW.3 and produced 3 documents as per Exs.P.20 to P.22.
In the crossexamination of PW.3 two documents are marked as Exs.R.1 and R.2.
On the other side, the Respondents did SCCH-25 not examine any witness nor produced any documents on their behalf.
9. Heard the arguments of both Counsel and perused the materials on record.

The counsel for the petitioner has relied upon the decision AIR 2019 SC (SUPP) 906 : Magma Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs.
Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram and Ors.

10. My finding to the above issues are as follows: Issue Nos.1 & 2 : In the affirmative Issue No.3 :
Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.4 : As per final order for the Following:
REASONS 11. Issue No.1:
It is the case of the Petitioners that, the Petitioners are the Mother and Father of the deceased - Arun Kumar H.R. and in support of the said claim they have examined 2nd petitioner as PW.1.
The PW.1 has specifically deposed this relationship in his chiefexamination.

Apart from that,
to SCCH-25 prove the relationship, the Petitioners have produced the copies of Aadhar Cards of themselves and deceased, death certificate of deceased, family Ration card and school admission register extract of the deceased as per Exs.P.12, P.16 to P.19.

In Ex.P.12/Aadhar Card of the petitioner No.2 his father's name is mentioned as Doddarangaiah and in the Aadhar card of the petitioner No.1 her husband's name is mentioned as Rangaswamaiah who is the petitioner No.2.
In the Ex.P16/death certificate of the deceased his parents name mentioned and they are none other than petitioners.
In the Ex.P.17/Aadhar card of the deceased his father's name is mentioned as Rangaswamaiah who is the petitioner No.2.
In the Ex.P.18/Ration Card, wherein the names of the petitioner Nos.1 and 2 and the deceased are mentioned.
In Ex.P.19/school admission register extract of deceased his father's and mother's name is mentioned as Rangaswamappa and Gangalakshmamma who is the petitioner Nos.1 and 2.

The Ex.P.10 PM report and inquest mahazar as per Ex.P.9 are produced, in the inquest mahazar SCCH-25 the name of father of the deceased is shown as Rangaswamaiah and Ex.P.6 charge sheet also shows that petitioners are the father and mother of the deceased, which affirms the case of the petitioners.
Further, these documents are public documents and they have got initial presumptive value under law.
These documents have not been seriously disputed by the Respondents.
The Respondents have not produced any contrary documents to dispute and rebut the contents of documents produced by the Petitioners.

As such,
there are no reasons to discard the oral and documentary evidence produced by the Petitioners.
Under such circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 and documents, this court is of the opinion that the Petitioners are the parents of the deceased.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.

12. Issue No.2: The Petitioners to prove that the accident was occurred due the actionable negligence on part of the driver of the SCCH-25 Goods Canter bearing Reg.No.KA5320D3899 has got examined 2nd petitioner as PW.1 and produced 9 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.6 and P.9 to P.11.

The PW.1 has specifically deposed in his evidence that the driver of the Goods Canter bearing Reg.No.KA20D3899 driven by its driver at a very high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endangering to human life came from behind and dashed to his son who was going to his garden on the left side of the road as a pedestrian.
The respondent No.1 has denied the case of the petitioners and involvement of the offending vehicle.
In the crossexamination of PW.1 nothing worth is elicited to disbelieve the alleged manner of accident.
13. The petitioners have also examined Mr.Ranganath - eye witness as PW.2.
PW.2 has deposed that he witnessed the accident.

In the crossexamination of PW.2 it is elicited that he lodged the first information before the police, the contents of first Smt. Gangalakshmamma vs Sbi Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88583706/
4 information are correct, the deceased is his sister's son, he did not sustain any injury, on the date of SCCH-25 accident he was proceeding towards his farm at 5.15am and the deceased was also with him, the Ex.P.5 sketch is correct, the said road was a highway, they were proceeding in the footpath mud road beside the tar road, on the left side of the said road his farm/land comes, Canter Lorry dashed from behind, the deceased was in his right side.

sentences.text: The other suggestions with regard to negligence on the part of the deceased are denied by the witness.
14. The Respondent No.1 have not led any contrary evidence to disprove the case of the petitioners with regard to occurrence of the alleged accident.
In the cross examination of PW.1 nothing worth is elicited to disprove the case of the petitioners with regard to alleged manner of accident.

Further,
the documents produced by the Petitioner such as the FIR in Cr.No.132/2020 of Kunigal Police Station with FIS, spot mahazar, seizure mahazar, spot sketch, MVA report, Inquest mahazar, PM report and charge sheet as per Exs.P.1 to P.6 and P.9 to P.11, which are all SCCH-25 public documents and have got initial presumptive value under law.
These documents fully and completely corroborated with the evidence of Pws.1 and 2.

In the charge sheet the PW.2's name is also forthcoming and police documents clearly show that the PW.1 and the deceased were proceeding by walk on the left side of road, which is not disproved by the respondent No.1 by leading cogent evidence.

The investigation officer in crime No.132/2020 of Kunigal had conducted the investigation in detail and filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending Goods Canter vehicle holding that the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Goods Canter vehicle.
Therefore, there are no reasons to discard the evidence of Pws.1, 2 and the documents produced.
Further, the PM report produced as per Ex.P.10 clearly shows the cause of death is 'hemorrhage shock due to poly trauma to limbs and head injury sustained'.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence coupled with the Exs.P.1 to P.6 and P.9 to P.11, this Court/Tribunal is of SCCH-25 the opinion that the driver of the offending Goods Canter bearing No.Reg.No.KA20D3899 driven it with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endangering to human life and caused the accident, result of which deceased Arun Kumar H.R.
sustained grievous head injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 is in the affirmative.
15. Issue No. 3:
The PW.1 has specifically deposed before this court that due to the untimely death of the deceased they have lost the bread earner of the family and loving son.
He has further deposed that they have spent Rs.80,000/ towards death related ceremonies.
This court while discussing the issue No.2 has come to the conclusion that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligence of the driver of the offending Goods Canter.
Under such circumstances, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation.
SCCH-25 Monthly income 16.

According to the Petitioners the deceased was working as a Salesman in the 'ESSAR OIL LIMITED', Sri Venkateshwara (Essar Bunk) Enterprises and he was getting salary of Rs.30,000/
per month including incentives.

In this regard, the Petitioners have produced offer letter dated 25.04.2020 issued by Sri.Venkateshwara Enterprises to the deceased, Employee ID of the deceased issued by Sri.Venkateshwara Enterprises and Two RTCs of Sy.No.30/16 and 30/17 of Smt. They have also examined Mr.Krishnaraja Nayak - Manager of Venkateshwara Enterprises as PW.3 and produced 3 documents as per Exs.P.20 to P.22.

The PW.3 has deposed that on 25.04.2020 the deceased was appointed to their Enterprises as salesman and the deceased joined to the said work on 01.05.2020 after receipt of appointment order, a sum of Rs.3,60,000/ was fixed as annual income of the deceased and the deceased did not turnup to the work from 23.05.2020 and they got information that he met with SCCH-25 an accident and hence they paid salary of 22 days in cash to the father of the deceased.

In his cross examination it is elicited that in their limited company totally 15 members were working and after Covid 11 members are working, they maintained the wages register, they also take signature of the employee in the register for having paid the salary.
The Exs.P.13 and P.21 are one and the same but the Ex.P.13 does not bear the signature of the deceased, in Ex.P.22 the PA stands for Pump Assistant.

Further elicited that in their company four categories of workers are there which is Manager, Cashier, Petrol Filling Salesman, Pump Assistant whose salary is Rs.40,000/,
Rs.35,000/, Rs.30,000/ and Rs.20,000/ respectively.

The witness admits that only on 01.05.2020 the deceased joined for work and prior to that the deceased was not working with them,
in the attendance register of March 2020 and April 2020 there is a name as Arunk Kumar at Sl.Nos.13, 12 respectively which is as per Exs.R.1 and R.2, to the front side of the said serial numbers it is mentioned as PA means Pump Assistant and the SCCH-25 witness denied the suggestion that in May 2020 attendance in front of the name of Arun Kumar the PA is strike out and written as Arun Kumar H.R..
17.

On perusal of Ex.P.13/Employment offer letter there is a offer to the name of Arun Kumar H.R.
for the position of Salesman in the Sri.Venkateshwara Enterprises.
In Ex.P.14 Employee ID the name of the employee shown as Arun Kumar/Salesman.
The Ex.P.15/RTC extracts are not standing in the name of the deceased and hence not considered.

The Ex.P.20 alleged to have issued by Preetham, Proprietor of Sri.Venkateshwara Enterprises (ESSAR OIL Ltd.,), but no document is produced to prove that Mr.Preetham is the Proprietor of the said company.
On perusal of Ex.P.22 (the attendant register extract of May 2020) at Sl.No.12 after the name 'Arun Kumar' the 'H R' is over written on 'PA'.

When this is compared with Exs.R.1 and R.2 which is marked in the cross examination of PW.3 it is clear that at Sl.No.12 and at Sl.No.13 of Exs.R.1 and R.2 SCCH-25 there is a name of one Arun Kumar PA.

As per the PW.3 himself the deceased was not working in their company in the months of March and April 2020 but only joined in the month of May 2020 then when this is coupled with the strike out and correction made in Ex.P.22 is appreciated it is clear that one person by name Arun Kumar was working in the company of PW.3 as Pump Assistant and his name is only corrected in the Ex.P.22 as 'Arun Kumar H R', which clearly shows that the Ex.P.22 is created document and impersonated in the name of deceased by misusing the earlier employee name and further makes it clear that to that effect the PW.3 has given false evidence before this court only to help the petitioners to get higher compensation.

Therefore, the said documents produced at Exs.P.13 to 15, P.21 and P.22 are not helpful to the petitioners to prove the alleged income of the deceased as the Exs.R.1 and R.2 supports the defence of the respondent No.1 to prove that the said documents are created by the petitioners.
Therefore, in the absence of proof for income of SCCH-25 deceased, the version of the Petitioners that the deceased was earning Rs.30,000/ per month is not acceptable.
Under such circumstances, this court has to consider the income of the deceased notionally for calculating the compensation.

sentences.text: The accident took place in the year 2020.

Therefore, having regard to the age of the deceased, and also relying on the decision of Hon'ble H.C. in the case of Sumangala & Others and Ramanagouda & Anr., in MFA No:202534/2019(MVC) wherein the notified notional income chart of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is considered for fixing the notional income and accordingly the monthly notional income of the deceased is considered as Rs.14,500/ per month.
Age of the deceased:
18.
In so far as age of the deceased is concerned, the Petitioner has produced copy of Aadhar Card of the deceased as per Ex.P.17.
As per Ex.P.17, the date of birth of the SCCH-25 deceased mentioned as 28.04.1998.
The accident was occurred on 23.05.2020.
As such, his age was 22 years as on the date of his death and accordingly, his age is considered 22 years.
i) LOSS OF DEPENDENCY:
As per principles of law laid down in the case of Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation, appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 18.

entities.text: Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, the deceased has Mother and Father who is the present petitioners.
The PW.1 Sri.Rangaswamaiah in his cross examination stated that he is doing Agriculture work and has 20 Guntas of land which is as Ex.P.15 and as per that they grown ragi.
From this it is clear that petitioner No.2 was depending on the income of the deceased.
Therefore the Petitioner No.1 is considered as the Sole Dependant of the deceased Arun Kumar H.R..

It is relevant to note that as per the recent decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in special leave petition No. 25590/2014 between National SCCH-25 Insurance Company Vs Pranay Sethi and others and other connected petitions, even in case of the self employed and fixed salary also the deceased is entitled for future prospects.

entities.text: National SCCH-25 Insurance Company Vs Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As mentioned above, in the present case since the deceased is less than 40 years age, 40% future prospects have to be added to his monthly income.
However, as the deceased is a bachelor, as per the Sarala Verma case, 1/2 of his income has to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
If 40% income is added to his monthly income, it comes around Rs.20,300/ (Rs.14,500/ + Rs.5,800/) and if 50% is deducted towards his living and personal expenses, balance comes to Rs.10,150/.

Therefore, the total loss of dependency would be Rs.21,92,400/ (Rs.10,150/ X 12 X 18 = Rs.21,92,400/).
ii) TRANSPORTATION AND FUNERAL EXPENSES AND LOSS TO THE ESTATE:

In so far as the funeral and transportation expenses are concerned, the Petitioners have deposed that they have SCCH-25 spent a sum of Rs.90,000/ towards transportation of dead body and funeral obsequies.
But, there is no document produced in this regard.
However, looking into the facts and circumstances of the case, it would be appropriate to award compensation of Rs.20,000/ towards funeral and transportation expenses.
If the deceased was alive he would have certainly saved some amount out of his living and personal expenses and created an estate in favour of the Petitioners.

Therefore, the Petitioners are entitled for Rs.20,000/ under the head of loss to the estate.
iii) CONSORTIUM:
The Petitioners being father and mother have lost their loving son and hence they are entitled to get compensation under parental consortium.
Therefore, the petitioners are entitled for a sum of Rs.80,000/ (Rs.40,000/ each) under the head of Consortium.

Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of a sum of Rs.23,12,400/.

sentences.text: In so far as liability is concerned, as discussed above the Respondent No.1 has failed to prove its defence about false implication of the offending vehicle and breach of policy conditions and therefore the respondents being the insurer and the insured of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
However, as the policy is existed, hence the respondent No.1 being the insurer is to indemnify the Respondent No.2 and directed to pay compensation to the petitioners.

Though the Petitioners have claimed compensation of Rs.70,00,000, but they are entitled only for a sum of Rs.23,12,400/ with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed in part.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.3 is partly in the affirmative.
SCCH-25 20. Issue No.4

: In view of the findings of the above issue Nos.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of Rs.23,12,400/ (Rupees Twenty Three Lakhs Twelve Thousand and Four Hundred Only) along with interest @ of 6% p.a., from the date of Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

However, the Respondent No.1/Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners and is directed to deposit the award amount and interest before this Tribunal within 60 days from the date of this Judgement.
SCCH-25 On deposit of the award amount and interest, 20% shall be deposited in the name of the Petitioner No.1 in any N/S bank for a period of 3 years and Rs.40,000/
shall be released in the name of the Petitioner No.2 and entire balance amount shall be released to the petitioner No.1 with proper identification and due acknowledgment as per Rules.
The Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1000/.
Draw Award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The Respondents have not produced any contrary documents to dispute and rebut the contents of documents produced by the Petitioners.
As such,
there are no reasons to discard the oral and documentary evidence produced by the Petitioners.
Under such circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 and documents, this court is of the opinion that the Petitioners are the parents of the deceased.
As per the PW.3 himself the deceased was not working in their company in the months of March and April 2020 but only joined in the month of May 2020 then when this is coupled with the strike out and correction made in Ex.P.22 is appreciated it is clear that one person by name Arun Kumar was working in the company of PW.3 as Pump Assistant and his name is only corrected in the Ex.P.22 as 'Arun Kumar H R', which clearly shows that the Ex.P.22 is created document and impersonated in the name of deceased by misusing the earlier employee name and further makes it clear that to that effect the PW.3 has given false evidence before this court only to help the petitioners to get higher compensation.
Therefore, the said documents produced at Exs.P.13 to 15, P.21 and P.22 are not helpful to the petitioners to prove the alleged income of the deceased as the Exs.R.1 and R.2 supports the defence of the respondent No.1 to prove that the said documents are created by the petitioners.
Therefore, in the absence of proof for income of SCCH-25 deceased, the version of the Petitioners that the deceased was earning Rs.30,000/ per month is not acceptable.
At the time of accident the deceased was a Smt. Gangalakshmamma vs Sbi Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88583706/
6 young aged person.
The accident took place in the year 2020.
As per Ex.P.17, the date of birth of the SCCH-25 deceased mentioned as 28.04.1998.
The accident was occurred on 23.05.2020.
As such, his age was 22 years as on the date of his death and accordingly, his age is considered 22 years.
As per principles of law laid down in the case of Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation, appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 18.
From this it is clear that petitioner No.2 was depending on the income of the deceased.
Therefore the Petitioner No.1 is considered as the Sole Dependant of the deceased Arun Kumar H.R..
However, as the deceased is a bachelor, as per the Sarala Verma case, 1/2 of his income has to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
If the deceased was alive he would have certainly saved some amount out of his living and personal expenses and created an estate in favour of the Petitioners.
The Petitioners being father and mother have lost their loving son and hence they are entitled to get compensation under parental consortium.
However, as the policy is existed, hence the respondent No.1 being the insurer is to indemnify the Respondent No.2 and directed to pay compensation to the petitioners.
